trap-nonspeakable.notes: pass. THREE FINDINGS, none fixed inline. (1) UNDECLARED VARIABLE t, MIXED WITH q IN THE SAME BLOCK. Regime 2 says coefficients are 'exact Laurent polynomials in Z[t, t^{-1}]', and the chaining section uses c_w(t), tr_alt(t), net(t) and the alternating weight (-t^{-2})^{l(w)} — while the optimisation section writes the Hecke relation with q, sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1}) sigma_i + 1. t is never defined. It is inferable: the sibling rem:kummer-shell-closure writes the same objects over Z[qcheck^{+-1}] with qcheck = q^{1/2} and the alternating weight (-q^{-1})^{l(w)}, and -t^{-2} = -q^{-1} exactly when t = q^{1/2} — so t is qcheck. But the reader has to reconstruct that from another block, and AGENTS.md 7a reserves against t as a polynomial variable (Jones is J_K(q), never V_K(t)). Proposed: write qcheck throughout, or state 't := q^{1/2}' once. (2) FLOAT FALLBACK, against the NO-FLOAT64 directive. The block's closing sentence prescribes 'a per-length accumulation float engine' for A > 20, and the sibling kummer block likewise has 'The float engine serves as a cross-check at q_0'. AGENTS.md's precision section (STRICT, 2026-08-18) forbids computing in float in computations/ and says a float64 input poisons the whole result; a per-length accumulation over A > 20 terms is exactly the aggregate-error case it names. Whether the engine actually exists is outside what I could check from the .md, but the block prescribes it. (3) UNDEFINED PARAMETERS c and d: the bottleneck paragraph characterises neutron-neutron crossings by 'c = 1, d = -(q - q^{-1})', referring back to the transfer matrices T(c_j, d_j) of Regime 1, which are named but never given. Lesser note: the scalability table's 'Coefficients' column holds magnitudes (10^12, 10^17, 10^22, > 10^38) in four rows and a count, O(A^2), in the fifth.
